backdrop.purpose: What the overlay dims the host page to.

canvas.purpose: The ground behind panels: overlay body, main column, exported report body.

surface.purpose: Cards, tables, panels, the side navigation, the top bar.

surface-raised.purpose: Menus and popovers that sit above a card.

sunken.purpose: Table heads, inset rows, hover fills.

ink-faint.purpose: Meta, hints, placeholders; 5.5:1 and the documented floor.

line.purpose: The 1px hairline between rows and around cards.

brand.purpose: Active navigation, primary buttons, focus ring, progress fill, surveyed coverage, the brand mark. Never severity.

brand-strong.purpose: The hover and pressed state of every violet fill; hover deepens rather than lightens.

brand-soft.purpose: The tinted ground for selected navigation, active lenses, the scope banner and the selected row.

brand-line.purpose: The hairline that pairs with the violet wash.

brand-text.purpose: The primary as text; 7.3:1 on surface. The fill value is never used as text.

focus.purpose: The 2px focus outline on every interactive element.

on-primary.purpose: The ink that sits on a violet fill and on the solid critical severity badge. White is the only value that clears 4.5:1 on #7350F5, which is why the primary is this violet and not a brighter one.

critical.purpose: Failure notices, danger buttons, broken status, the high-severity badge label.

warn.purpose: Review notices, partial coverage, unestablished evidence.

ok.purpose: Healthy status, established confidence, resolved findings.

info.purpose: Informational chips; deliberately the same violet as primary-as-text.

info-soft.purpose: The wash beneath info text, and the neutral track under severity and coverage bars.

sev-critical.purpose: Severity fill, top of the ramp; the one solid severity badge fill, white on it.

sev-high.purpose: Severity fill: bars, rails, dots, legend swatches.

sev-info.purpose: Severity fill, bottom of the ramp.

display.purpose: Stat-strip figures where the figure is the point; 26px/650 tabular at -0.03em. The largest type in the product is a number.

display-compact.purpose: The same figure in a dense grid — the progress view six-tile strip, the discipline section stats; 22px/650 at -0.02em.

headline.purpose: One step, 18px/650 at -0.02em: the main-column page title, the inspected pattern title, the side panel idle heading, the report masthead. The build had carried 17, 18 and 19px within two pixels of each other, which was accumulation rather than hierarchy.

display-panel.purpose: The side panel figure at 20px/650; a 300-420px column cannot spend 26px on a number.

headline-panel.purpose: The side panel heading at 15px/650. The panel owns only these two top-of-ramp steps; everything below the top is shared with the console.

title.purpose: Card heads, section headings, finding titles, button labels; 13-13.5px/600.

body.purpose: Lede and descriptive copy on the console surfaces; 12.5-13px/400, capped at 74ch.

body-public.purpose: The public scanner reads at 16px/400. A landing page is read at arm’s length; the console does not inherit it.

body-coach.purpose: The walkthrough card at 14.5px/400. The coach is read, not scanned — one step up from the console working density.

body-panel.purpose: The side panel root size at 14px/400, which most of that surface then steps down from.

meta.purpose: Counts, hints, table heads, foot notes; 11.5-12.5px/500.

label.purpose: The only uppercase role: 11px/650 at 0.07-0.09em, provenance micro-labels only (SCANNER EVIDENCE, LUMEN INTERPRETATION). 11px is the floor and the label sits exactly on it; the step was 10.5px until a detector pass called it.

mono.purpose: IBM Plex Mono at 11-12.5px for URLs, rule ids, coverage detail, evidence values.

fonts.name: IBM Plex Sans
fonts.value: self-hosted variable woff2, weight axis 400-700, font-display:swap; latin and latin-ext subsets in packages/ui/fonts/, declared once in packages/ui/fonts.css
fonts.purpose: Every surface. 650 is a real weight because the build is variable, not a synthetic bold rounded to 700. The fallback stack is load-bearing rather than decoration: system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica Neue, sans-serif.

fonts.name: IBM Plex Mono
fonts.value: self-hosted woff2 at 400 and 600, latin subset, font-display:swap
fonts.purpose: The sans’s own sibling, so a rule id beside a sentence is one voice at a different width. Fallback: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, SF Mono, Menlo, Consolas, monospace.

fonts.name: Delivery
fonts.value: packages/ui/fonts.css holds every src behind a __LUMEN_FONT_BASE__ placeholder; three paths substitute their own base
fonts.purpose: Compiled sheets link fonts/ relatively. The injected overlay and coach cannot declare @font-face inside a shadow root, so the content script registers the faces on the host document via chrome.runtime.getURL() (lumenFontFaceTemplate / ensureLumenFontFaces in apps/extension/content.js) and removes the style when the last Lumen root closes. packages/crawl/report.js embeds the subsets as data: URIs. Nothing fetches a font CDN, and no surface is the only place a src is written.

shadows.name: ambient
shadows.purpose: Cards, tiles, buttons, inputs. Barely visible by design; the tonal step does the work.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: The marginally lifted step above ambient.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: The fixed overlay workspace, the columns menu, modal shells. Reserved for elements actually detached from the document.

shadows.name: severity-rail
shadows.purpose: Severity carried as a 3px inset rail on the leading edge of a finding row, over the ambient shadow.

shadows.name: spotlight
shadows.purpose: The coach spotlight: a full-viewport scrim punched by a white ring and a 5px violet ring. The ring is the meaning; there is no bloom behind it.

motion.name: control
motion.purpose: Button, chip, lens and table-row state changes.

motion.name: disclosure
motion.purpose: Chevron and details-marker rotation on expand.

motion.name: progress
motion.value: transform .3s ease, scaleX from a left origin
motion.purpose: Crawl progress and coverage fills. Animating transform rather than width keeps the fill off the layout path; the script sets style.transform = scaleX(pct/100).

motion.name: spotlight
motion.value: opacity .22s ease, transform .22s ease, top .16s ease, left .16s ease, width .16s ease, height .16s ease
motion.purpose: The coach spotlight travelling between elements.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Honoured in the overlay, the coach, the side panel and the web surface.

radii.name: xxs
radii.purpose: One job only: capping the outer end of the 3px severity rail, where any larger radius rounds a 3px bar into a lozenge.

radii.name: sm
radii.purpose: Buttons, inputs, selects, nav items, lens tabs, sunken evidence panels. --wqa-r-sm, the most used step in the build.

radii.name: md
radii.purpose: Cards, tables, panels, callouts. --wqa-r, the unsuffixed default.

radii.name: float
radii.purpose: Floating shells: the fixed overlay workspace and the walkthrough coach card.

radii.name: pill
radii.purpose: Counters, status pills, severity badges, progress and coverage bars, filter chips — things read as tokens rather than containers. --wqa-r-pill.

patterns.name: The inset left rail
patterns.purpose: Sanctioned. How severity stays legible without colour-coding the whole row; craft detectors read it as a side tab and that reading is wrong here.

patterns.name: The hatch
patterns.purpose: What was not surveyed. Never greyed out, never coloured as a failure.

patterns.name: The distribution rail
patterns.value: 10-12px pill bar segmented by the severity ramp with a tabular key beneath
patterns.purpose: Same device, same meaning, in the overlay Overview and the exported report.

patterns.name: The dot
patterns.value: 6-8px circle; the conditions mark is an 18px ringed dot with a 5px inset core
patterns.purpose: Confidence and state. Not-established swaps the core for a 2px dashed ring.

patterns.name: The one mark
patterns.value: 26-30px violet tile at 7-8px radius with a 2px white ring inset
patterns.purpose: The brand mark is a single construction everywhere: a lens.

surfaceTargets.name: Site Audit overlay
surfaceTargets.note: The fullest expression: 216px side nav, scrolling main column, stat strips, findings inspector, sortable data tables.

surfaceTargets.name: Side panel
surfaceTargets.note: The same system compressed to a 300-420px column; 14px gutters, 18px section gaps.

surfaceTargets.name: Public scanner
surfaceTargets.note: A single column inside a 1440px sheet; 16px body, read at arm’s length.

surfaceTargets.name: Exported client report
surfaceTargets.note: One self-contained HTML file that inlines tokens.css and redefines the palette inside @media print.

knownGaps: Confidence dots are drawn for confirmed, inferred and inconclusive only (.confidence-dot, apps/extension/content.js); corroborated has no drawn dot and falls through unstyled. DESIGN.md records the same gap inside The Closed Vocabulary Rule.

The primary as text survives in three places outside the overlay: .btn-brand and its hover in apps/extension/sidepanel.css, and .finding-actions .ask-frank in packages/ui/web.css with its mirror in apps/web/public/styles.css, all set color:var(--wqa-brand-strong) (#6741E8) on the violet wash (#1E1838), roughly 2:1. The Fill Is Not The Ink Rule names --wqa-brand-text (#A896FF) as the only violet that may follow color:, and the sidecar records the documented value.

Three frontmatter entries are documented as scale but have no custom property in packages/ui/tokens.css: rounded.float (12px, written literally on .workspace and .coach), rounded.xxs (2px, written literally on the severity rail cap), and colors.on-primary (#FFFFFF, written as the literal #fff at every use site).

The side panel carries ten distinct sizes between 11px and 20px, several of them half-pixel neighbours (11/11.5, 12/12.5, 13/13.5). DESIGN.md records this as an accumulation wanting a dedicated pass; the sidecar records the ramp, not the accumulation.

DESIGN.md still describes the stat strip as a 1px-gap grid with a 10.5px uppercase label over a 24-26px figure. The build draws a 14px-gap grid of hairlined surface cells with a 12.5px/500 sentence-case label over a 26px/650 figure, which is the reading that obeys The Sentence Case Rule and The 11px Floor Rule; the sidecar records the build.

The nav-item-active component in the DESIGN.md frontmatter sets textColor to colors.ink, and stat-tile to rounded.sm. The build draws .tab.active in --sa-primary-text (#A896FF) and the stat cell at 10px; the sidecar records the build.
notCanonized: The primary fill, or its deep hover value, used as text on the violet wash: a contrast defect, not a token pairing. Recorded as a gap so the remaining three sites get fixed, never as a sanctioned pairing.

The uppercase .crumb kicker above panel titles, prohibited by The Provenance Label Rule and the craft floor: it has been deleted from apps/extension/content.js, so it is neither a documented component nor a live gap.
Values seen once in the build — the 16px and 18px strays in the side panel, the 1180px and 720px reflows of the progress stat grid — are layout facts, not system steps.

components.name: Side Navigation
components.description: The overlay 216px rail: site identity, grouped destinations with right-aligned tabular counts, primary action pinned to the foot. Active fills the violet wash and takes the violet TEXT value (#A896FF); the fill value is never used as a label.

components.name: Lens Tab / Filter Chip
components.description: The findings lenses and filter chips: transparent at rest with a faint label, flipping to violet wash, violet hairline and violet-text label when active.

components.name: Severity Badge and Status Pill
components.description: Pill, 11.5px/600, capitalised. High, medium and low take the semantic wash with a ramp-tinted hairline; critical is the one solid ramp fill under on-primary white. Status pills use the same silhouette for healthy, broken, and for blocked and inconclusive, which share the neutral info wash on both the overlay and the exported report — a destination that refuses an automated request is a limit on coverage, not a defect in the site.

components.description: A finding carries its severity as a 3px inset rail on the leading edge, its confidence as a dot plus a word from the closed vocabulary, and nothing else coloured. Every rail step reads its own sealed-ramp value, critical included. Hover strengthens the hairline.

narrative.overview:
An audit is an investigation in progress, not a report that appears at the end. This world refuses the light document page the category ships — Sitebulb's and Semrush's white sheet of tables — and commits to the dark instrument surface a consultant leaves open on a second monitor while a crawl runs. Evidence glows against it; the ground itself never competes.

This direction was pinned by the operator, who supplied six mockups and asked for the product to be rebuilt against them. It replaces the light "category standard, played straight" world recorded in the previous version of this document, which had explicitly reserved that exit for them. Sitebulb and Semrush remain the bar for density, severity discipline and completeness; they are no longer the reference for how Lumen looks.

The surface is a near-black canvas (#0E0E14) with slightly lighter panels on it, hairlines a shade above the ground doing the structural work, and one violet primary carrying the product's own voice. Density is high and deliberate: 12.5–13.5px body text, 11–12.5px table cells, 8px and 14px gaps, tabular figures everywhere a number can be compared to another number. The Site Audit overlay is the fullest expression — a 216px left navigation grouped into destinations, a scrolling main column, stat strips, the site-conditions readout, a master–detail findings inspector and sortable data tables. The side panel is the same system compressed to a 300–420px column, and the exported client report is the same system in one emailable file.
keyCharacteristics: One violet primary (#7350F5) that never means severity
A sealed five-step severity ramp used only for severity
Contrast computed, not eyeballed: every text token clears 4.5:1 on all four grounds
One self-hosted superfamily — IBM Plex Sans and its own monospace sibling — across every surface
Depth from the ground stepping lighter and from hairlines, not from shadow
Left navigation grouped into destinations, a scrolling main column, a 900px fold to a horizontal strip
Tabular figures, and hatching for what was not surveyed

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Violet is the product speaking — navigation, primary actions, focus, selection, progress. It never means severity. A red button that is not destructive is a bug; a violet element that encodes an audit result is the same bug in the other direction.

rules.name: The Fill Is Not The Ink Rule
rules.body: --wqa-brand (#7350F5) is a fill: backgrounds, borders, focus rings, bars. As text it measures about 4.1:1 on the surface and 4.4:1 on the canvas, and both fail. --wqa-brand-text (#A896FF, 7.3:1) is the primary as text and is the only one of the two that may follow color:. This was violated in sixteen places across three surfaces before a sidecar regeneration compared the build against this document and found them.

rules.name: The Sealed Ramp Rule
rules.body: --wqa-sev-* exists for severity and nothing else. Nothing outside a severity bar, rail, dot or legend swatch may take a value from it, and severity may not be expressed in any colour outside it. scripts/check.mjs fails the build on color:var(--sa-sev-*).

rules.name: The Computed Contrast Rule
rules.body: Every text token clears 4.5:1 on backdrop, canvas, surface and sunken. --wqa-ink-faint (#8B8BA3, 5.5:1) is the floor — it must not be darkened, and no new text token may land below it. Each semantic text colour clears 4.5:1 on its own wash, which is why critical text is #FF6B78 rather than the ramp's #E14356.

rules.name: The One Palette Rule
rules.body: packages/ui/tokens.css is the only place a colour is named. First-party pages link the compiled sheet. The three surfaces that cannot — the Site Audit overlay, the walkthrough coach and the exported report — have the token block injected at build or render time. scripts/check.mjs fails the build if the overlay redeclares any value tokens.css already names.

rules.name: The Hatch Rule
rules.body: What was not surveyed is drawn with the 45° hatch (repeating-linear-gradient(45deg,transparent 0 6px,rgba(233,233,242,.07) 6px 7px)), not greyed out and not coloured as a failure. Not knowing is not the same as being broken, and that distinction stays visual.

rules.name: The Provenance Label Rule
rules.body: The uppercase tracked micro-label exists for one job: marking whether the sentence under it is measurement or reading. On this surface a reader must always be able to tell the scanner's words from Lumen's. It is not a decorative eyebrow, and it is not used above ordinary headings.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: One superfamily, declared once in packages/ui/tokens.css and inherited everywhere else. There is no second family anywhere in the product.

rules.name: The Self-Hosted Rule
rules.body: The faces ship with the product (packages/ui/fonts/, SIL OFL 1.1) and are never fetched from a font CDN. Lumen audits sites for third-party requests and privacy exposure; a tool that does that while calling out to Google Fonts to render its own name has not taken its own advice. Self-hosting also means the extension works offline and a client's exported report renders correctly on a plane.

rules.name: The Three Delivery Paths Rule
rules.body: Same files, three ways of reaching them. Document surfaces (public scanner, side panel) link a compiled sheet beside its own fonts/ directory, written by scripts/build-css.mjs. Injected surfaces (overlay, coach) cannot declare @font-face inside a shadow root at all, because font faces resolve against the document and never the shadow tree, so the content script registers one inert <style> on the host page with chrome.runtime.getURL() paths and removes it when the last Lumen root closes; the host page CSP decides whether the files load, which is why the fallback stack is load-bearing rather than decoration. The emailed report embeds the four latin subsets as data: URIs, about 140KB, because it is opened from file:// months later on a machine that has never seen Lumen. No surface may be the only place a src is written: packages/ui/fonts.css holds the rules and each path substitutes its own base.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Any number a reader might compare against another number carries font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums — stat strips, counts, table cells, pager labels, history rows.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings, badges and buttons are sentence case or capitalised, never letterspaced uppercase. Uppercase at 0.07–0.09em tracking is reserved for the provenance micro-label.

rules.name: The 11px Floor Rule
rules.body: 11px is the smallest type in the product, and the provenance label sits exactly on it. Functional text below 11px fails on high-DPI screens and small viewports, and a letterspaced micro-label is functional text — it names where a sentence came from. Being on the documented ramp is not an exemption: lowering the ramp step to legitimise an 8px label launders the token, not the legibility. The label step was 10.5px until a detector pass called it, and moving the step was the right answer rather than exempting the one surface that got measured.

rules.name: The 900px Fold Rule
rules.body: At max-width:900px the overlay's side navigation becomes a horizontal scrolling strip above the content: destinations go inline, the group labels hide, the nav foot moves to the row end, and the site-conditions row drops from a four-column grid to label-over-detail. The fold changes arrangement, never content.

rules.name: The Tonal-Step-First Rule
rules.body: Structure comes from the ground stepping and from 1px #2E2E3D hairlines. A shadow never substitutes for a border, and no surface takes a second border where a hairline divider will do.

rules.name: The Ring, Not the Bloom Rule
rules.body: The spotlight's violet ring carries meaning: this is the element. A soft wide glow behind it carries none and is not drawn.

rules.name: The Floating-Means-Floating Rule
rules.body: The deep shadow is reserved for elements actually detached from the document — the fixed workspace, the coach, popovers, dialogs. A card in the flow never takes it.

rules.name: The One Mark Rule
rules.body: The brand mark is a single construction everywhere: a 26–30px violet tile at 7–8px radius with a 2px white ring inset inside it — a lens. Three near-variants of a logo read as three products, so there is now one.

rules.name: The Shortened URL Rule
rules.body: No results table prints the crawled site's own origin. Same-site URLs render as their path; external URLs keep host plus path, because there the host is the information. Every shortened cell carries the full URL in its title, and links still navigate to the absolute URL — shortening is a display rule, never a loss of data.

rules.name: The Lens, Not Verdict Rule
rules.body: Lumen priority is presented as a lens over the scanner's labels and says so on the screen, in a standing note beside the tabs. Ordering may change; severity, confidence and counts render exactly as recorded. No discipline is promoted for being easy to detect.

rules.name: The No Score Rule
rules.body: The conditions readout carries no score, grade or index — in the overlay or in the exported report. Each row states what was observed plus the confidence that observation supports. A single number would hide the evidence behind it.

rules.name: The Closed Vocabulary Rule
rules.body: Confidence is rendered only as one of the four levels defined in packages/findings/confidence.js: confirmed, corroborated, inferred, inconclusive. Never invent a fifth word to soften a finding — normalizeConfidence() coerces an unknown word to its fallback, so inventing one upgrades the finding and manufactures certainty. Never express "unavailable" or "not applicable" as confidence; that is coverage.

rules.name: The Withheld-Is-Not-Zero Rule
rules.body: When a comparison cannot be made — a sitemap coverage figure the page limit made meaningless, a destination a platform refused to serve — the readout prints an em dash and the reason, never a zero. A withheld number rendered as 0 reads as agreement, which is the most expensive lie this product can tell.

rules.name: The Paper Half Rule
rules.body: The exported report ships a print stylesheet that redefines the palette tokens inside @media print — one override, not a patch per class, because every rule already reads a token. On paper the ground is white, the inks are the light-world semantic values, every destination is shown at once, and the severity fills carry print-color-adjust:exact so meaning survives the browser stripping backgrounds.

rules.name: The Document Cannot Contradict The Screen Rule
rules.body: Four things are shared modules with exactly one definition each: the palette (packages/ui/tokens.css), the discipline taxonomy (packages/findings/disciplines.js), the priority order (packages/findings/priority.js), and the fix sentences (packages/findings/rule-guidance.js). A consultant walks a client through the screen and then sends them the exported file; it may not call the same finding by a different name, file it under a different area, or put something else first.

dos: Do use violet (#7350F5) for navigation, primary action, focus, selection and progress — and only for those.
Do carry elevation with the tonal step and a hairline. On this ground a drop shadow reads as smudge.

Do keep the scroll container full-width and centre content with padding. A max-width + margin:0 auto column that is also the scroller renders its scrollbar mid-panel against the column edge, which reads as a stray second scrollbar.
Do take severity colour from --wqa-sev-* and semantic text colour from --wqa-critical / --wqa-warn / --wqa-ok, which are contrast-cleared on their own washes.
Do treat --wqa-ink-faint (#8B8BA3, 5.5:1) as the lightest-duty text in the product and never go below it.
Do hatch what was not surveyed, and state coverage limits in words next to it.
Do give every comparable number font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.
Do carry severity as the 3px inset leading rail, and confidence as a dot plus a word from the closed vocabulary.
Do keep the 4 / 8 / 12 / 16 / 24 spacing rhythm and the 10px-card / 8px-control / 999px-token radius split.
Do put a 2px solid #7350F5 focus ring on every interactive element.
Do reach for the shared module when two surfaces need the same fact — palette, taxonomy, priority, guidance. A second copy is how they start disagreeing.
donts: Don't darken --wqa-ink-faint or introduce a text token below 4.5:1 on any of the four grounds.
Don't set a severity ramp value as text on a tint — the ramp is fills only.
Don't use red, amber or green for anything that is not a statement about the audited site; and don't use violet to encode an audit result.
Don't add a score, grade, index or single health number to the conditions readout or the report.
Don't invent a confidence word outside confirmed / corroborated / inferred / inconclusive.
Don't render a withheld comparison as a zero, or an unrun check as an empty section that reads clean.
Don't fetch the typeface from a CDN on any surface, and don't let an injected or emailed surface depend on a stylesheet it cannot link. The faces ship with the product.

Don't restate a palette value anywhere outside packages/ui/tokens.css. The exception is the print block in packages/crawl/report.js, which is the documented paper palette and exists because paper has its own inks.

Don't add kickers or eyebrow labels above headings. The uppercase micro-label marks provenance and nothing else. The overlay carried an uppercase “Site audit / Findings” line directly above an <h1> reading “Findings”, inside a workspace whose header and left nav already said both — three statements of one fact, removed.
Don't ship hard offset shadows, glyph or emoji icons, or a system display face; icons are inline SVG stroked in currentColor.

Don't revert to The Category Standard, Played Straight (light #F6F7F9 canvas, white cards, indigo #4F46E5, color-scheme:light), and don't revive The Drawing Set or The Control Room before it. All three are retired.
